subject: Private VPC deployment — control/data plane diagram review
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@acme-payments.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Infra Team <infra@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: private VPC control/data plane diagrams for onboarding

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. We have an internal architecture review at Acme next week and the network/security reviewers asked for a clear control-plane vs data-plane diagram for the Redwood private deployment (VPC + on-prem attachment). They specifically asked for:

- single-page topology showing where control traffic terminates (control plane endpoints, regions)
- data-plane paths for inference traffic (egress rules, NAT/egress proxies)
- any required firewall rules, ports, and approximate CIDR blocks (placeholder ranges are fine)
- a short notes section describing KMS usage and audit log flow

Can you share a diagram we can drop into our packet and a short blurb they can reference? If there are known incompatibilities with our on-prem NAT gateways or restrictions (e.g., no outbound TLS interception), please flag those.

Appreciate it — we want to avoid a last-minute hold on the compliance review.

Thanks,
Alex Torres\Lead Infrastructure Engineer\Acme Payments

[Attachment: request-checklist.txt (text/plain)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private VPC control/data plane diagrams for onboarding

Alex — thanks, got it. Attaching a first-draft diagram and a two-paragraph summary that covers control/data separation, egress expectations, and KMS/audit flow. High-level notes below.

Key callouts (summary):
- Control plane: TLS-mutual authenticated control channel to Redwood-managed control endpoints in us-west-2 (default). Control plane traffic is management-only and runs over port 443 (mutual TLS). Customers can opt to run a private control plane in their VPC for air-gapped installations — see option B in the attached diagram.
- Data plane: Inference traffic terminates on customer-facing inference pods in your VPC (on-prem gateway or cloud attach). Egress to model artifacts and telemetry goes through customer-managed NAT/egress proxies. Recommend allowing outbound 443 to our egress hostnames; where limited, use a proxy with SNI passthrough for TLS.
- KMS & logs: Model keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM) when requested; audit logs stream to your SIEM via a push connector (we can provide a signed webhook endpoint).

Attachments: acme-vpc-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram, single page), egress-matrix-snippet.png (egress matrix excerpt).

I can hop on a 30-min sync if your reviewers want a walkthrough; otherwise accept this as a working artifact for the packet.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher\Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference\[Attachment: acme-vpc-diagram-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: egress-matrix-snippet.png (image/png)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private VPC control/data plane diagrams for onboarding

Thanks for the draft, Sean — good starting point. Quick internal redlines before we send to Acme: 

1) Control plane endpoint naming: call out fully-qualified hostnames (control.redwood-inference.com) and include fallback region endpoints (us-east-1) in the notes. That helps firewall rule reviewers.

2) Ports: control plane uses 443/HTTPS (mutual TLS), but add: health-check ping from control plane to agent uses TCP 5222 (short-lived) in the agent-hosted private option.

3) Egress matrix: add rows for telemetry (k8s metrics push) and model artifact download (S3-compatible endpoints). Mark telemetry as optional — customers can opt-out.

4) KMS: indicate whether envelope encryption is in-flight or at-rest; recommend we mark both and default to "customer-managed at rest" for Acme. Also add a one-line for rotation cadence (90 days suggested).

5) Diagram clarity: separate the "on-prem gateway" from the "cloud attach" lanes visually — reviewers get confused when both are visually adjacent.

If Karthik or Kim have infra-level constraints, please add inline notes. I can iterate quickly and send final to Alex.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole\Director, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: private VPC diagram + reviewer notes (control/data plane)

Alex — attaching the updated diagram and a short packet blurb (PDF). Changes from the draft: fully-qualified control hostnames, explicit port matrix, distinct lanes for on-prem gateway vs cloud attach, and a small telemetry opt-out note. We also included recommended CIDR placeholders you can hand to firewall reviewers.

Next steps:
- If this looks good, you can include acme-vpc-diagram-v1.pdf in the compliance packet.
- If your reviewers request tighter egress controls (no direct S3), we can provide an SFTP pull option for model artifacts and a signed attest for artifact checks.
- If you'd like, book 30 minutes on my calendar for a quick walkthrough (I kept availability next Tue/Wed morning).

Quoting Marissa's redlines below for traceability.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher\Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
